THIS IS NOT A PENDING RULING -- it is what itemtext_standard.md's 2026-09-08 ruling (irw#2121) prescribes: two instruments are in play whenever a study administers a translated adaptation and IRW ships the original-language wording as a stand-in, and the test is to go to the terms of the thing you actually copied. What IRW copied here is the English DASS-21, which is public domain, so it ships; the Greek translation's terms govern the Greek wording only, and they could not be located. Both of that ruling's limits are met: this is a straight translation and not a revision (Lyrakos et al. is titled a translation-and-validation study, and all 21 stems were checked against the English one by one), and the originator's own terms are quoted rather than asserted from an audit row. The only question left open is the UPGRADE: whether the Greek wording could itself move into the base fields, which needs the translators' terms or a ruling that the DASS site's "copied without restriction" reaches the translations it hosts. translation_source (no column in this file, see TODO.md): the official DASS-21 form, https://www2.psy.unsw.edu.au/dass/Download%20files/Dass21.pdf, fetched 2026-10-19, sha256 8644cc86534d397e371985d5b25422ba76c4cdae0a5aed8f1a4453c17a5cd393 -- instructions, all 21 stems and all four anchors are transcribed from that one form, so nothing here is IRW-authored and nothing is machine-translated.
